quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

60 Questions • Passing Score 50

questions.question: When driving behind a motorcycle in normal weather and traffic, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three to four seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep a distance of three to four seconds behind a motorcycle. This gives you more time to react if the motorcycle falls or stops suddenly. Extra distance helps you avoid hitting the rider.

questions.question: When you see a car coming toward you with bright headlights, what should you do?

options.text: Use your bright lights until the other car dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and then speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look away from the bright headlights and toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded while the other car passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not drink if you will drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road becomes slippery when wet.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing without traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this situation will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you approach an unmarked railroad crossing. Look both ways to make sure no trains are coming on any track. Stop if you see or hear a train. Wait for the train to pass before you cross.

questions.question: When do roads become very slippery?

options.text: After it has rained for an hour or more.
During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.

questions.correctAnswerText: During the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
questions.explanation: Roads are most slippery during the first 10 to 15 minutes of rain. Rain pushes oil from the asphalt to the road surface. Hot weather makes this worse because heat causes more oil to rise.

questions.question: What speed should you always travel at?

options.text: The same speed as the vehicles around you.
A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: A speed that fits the road and weather conditions.
questions.explanation: Drive at a speed that matches road conditions, weather, and the speed limit. Never drive faster than the speed limit. Slow down when road or weather conditions are not ideal.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Fines double in a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign alerts drivers that bicycles may cross the road ahead.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator gets stuck while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully without locking the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: If the accelerator sticks, turn off the ignition carefully. Move the switch just enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and move safely off the road.

questions.question: What do pentagonal signs indicate?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zones.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mark school zones. Be extra careful and watch for children and pedestrians near schools.

questions.question: What is the most common color for warning signs?
questions.correctAnswerText: Yellow.
questions.explanation: Most warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black markings. These signs warn you about unexpected conditions ahead.

questions.question: When parallel parking between two cars, what should you do first?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the left.
Turn your wheels to the right.
Pull up next to the car in front of the parking space.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull up next to the car in front of the parking space.
questions.explanation: After finding a parking space and signaling, stop next to the car in front of your desired spot. Then turn your wheels to park.

questions.question: When a solid yellow line and a broken yellow line mark the center, and the broken line is next to your lane, when can you pass?
questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic ahead is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to your lane means you can cross it to pass. You may pass only if there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: You are in the left lane and want to move to the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder.
Check mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders.
Check mirrors and signal, then change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Always check your mirrors and signal before changing lanes. Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move to check your blind spot.

questions.question: When traffic is moving at 50 to 55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:

options.text: Drive a few mph faster than other vehicles.
Drive at the same speed as the traffic around you.
Drive a few mph slower than other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive at the same speed as the traffic around you.
questions.explanation: Match the speed of traffic around you, as long as it is within the speed limit. Vehicles moving at the same speed in the same direction cannot hit each other. Crashes happen when vehicles travel at different speeds.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?

options.text: You can pass on the right when the road is clear.
You can pass on the left when the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass on the left when the road is clear.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to your side means you can cross it to pass. You may pass on the left when the road ahead is clear.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, how should you check for traffic?

options.text: Use your rearview and side mirrors.
Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder to see traffic when entering a freeway. This helps you spot vehicles in your blind spot.

questions.question: When entering a highway from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Speed up to get ahead of traffic.
Enter slowly to avoid other vehicles.
Stop first, then slowly enter traffic.
Speed up to match the traffic speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the traffic speed.
questions.explanation: Use the acceleration lane to speed up to match traffic. Signal, look for a gap, speed up, and merge safely into traffic.

questions.question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal, you should:

options.text: Merge in the direction the arrow points.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic pass.
Have the right-of-way and oncoming traffic must stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop if it is safe.
questions.explanation: A steady yellow arrow warns you that a red arrow is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on the freeway, you should NOT:

options.text: Continue driving and find another route.
Drive to the next exit and leave the freeway.
Back up on the road or shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Back up on the road or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway road or shoulder. Other drivers do not expect this and a crash will likely happen. Instead, continue to the next exit.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing.
questions.explanation: A five-sided yellow or yellow-green sign warns drivers of a school zone or school crossing.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: A speed that is faster than is safe and reasonable.
A speed that is safe for current conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must drive at a speed that is safe and reasonable. Adjust your speed based on traffic, pedestrians, weather, road conditions, and lighting. Always obey posted speed limits.

questions.question: At a "Yield" sign, you must:

options.text: Give the right-of-way to vehicles that could cause a collision.
Give the right-of-way only to vehicles on your right.
Always slow down and continue without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to vehicles that could cause a collision.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, slow down or stop if needed. Give the right-of-way to any vehicle that is close enough to cause a collision.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: A four-way intersection is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a four-way intersection is coming.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.correctAnswerText: Divided highway ends.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the divided highway is ending. Be ready to change lanes or adjust your position.

questions.question: If you park uphill on a street with a curb, set the parking brake and:

options.text: Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your wheels away from the curb. When parking uphill without a curb or parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb or road edge.

questions.question: In normal weather and traffic, keep at least this much distance between your vehicle and the one ahead:
questions.correctAnswerText: Two seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep a two-second distance in normal conditions. This gives you time to react to other drivers. Increase your distance in bad weather or heavy traffic.

questions.question: You must pull over and let an emergency vehicle pass:

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights, whether it is coming from behind or from the opposite direction.

questions.question: A driver license is a:
questions.correctAnswerText: Privilege.
questions.explanation: Driving is a privilege, not a right. All drivers must help keep roads safe. If you misuse this privilege, it can be taken away.

questions.question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, you must:

options.text: Flash your lights at oncoming traffic.
Use the lane for oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the lane for oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: To pass on a two-lane road, you must use the oncoming traffic lane. Only pass when it is safe and legal.

questions.question: A solid white line on the road's right edge that slants left means:
questions.correctAnswerText: The road narrows ahead.
questions.explanation: A solid line marks the road's edge. When this line angles toward the center, the road is getting narrower.

questions.question: If your wheels drop off the edge of the road, what should you do?

options.text: Wait until it is safe, then slowly move back onto the road.
Turn back onto the road right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until it is safe, then slowly move back onto the road.
questions.explanation: Do not turn back onto the road immediately. Instead, slow down, check traffic, and carefully return to the road when it is safe.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to stop for any train.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop for any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to stop for trains at railroad crossings without lights or gates. Only cross when your entire vehicle can fit on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand point upward. What does this mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn right.
questions.explanation: When a driver's left arm points upward, they plan to turn right. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: Which road is most likely to be slippery in cold weather after snow or rain?
questions.correctAnswerText: A road in shade
questions.explanation: Shaded areas on roads freeze first and thaw last in cold, wet weather. These areas can be icy when the rest of the road is not.

questions.question: What can a leaking exhaust system do?

options.text: Start grass fires on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make you sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes toxic gases and cools hot engine fumes. A leak releases harmful fumes that can make you sleepy or cause serious harm.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the center line in an intersection.
Look over your shoulder for blind spots.
Check for other drivers in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the center line in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spot and look for other drivers. Never change lanes or pass in an intersection.

questions.question: You can drive faster than the speed limit when passing another vehicle.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: Never exceed the speed limit, even when passing another vehicle.

questions.question: If a light shows both red and a green arrow, you cannot turn in the arrow's direction until the red light changes.
questions.correctAnswerText: False
questions.explanation: After yielding to traffic in the intersection or crosswalk, you may turn in the direction the green arrow points, even if other lights are red.

questions.question: When parallel parking downhill, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them toward the curb or road edge.
Turn them away from the curb or road edge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them toward the curb or road edge.
questions.explanation: When parking downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb. When parking uphill on a road without a curb, turn toward the edge. When parking uphill with a curb, turn away from the curb.

questions.question: If someone passes you in a no passing zone, what should you do?

options.text: Slow down so the other driver can safely return to your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down so the other driver can safely return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Help the passing vehicle return to your lane safely. This helps both drivers avoid hazards ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They prepare you for road hazards. This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: To turn quickly, where should your hands be on the steering wheel?

options.text: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: On opposite sides of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Place both hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel. This position lets you turn quickly and safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with yellow background and black markings. They alert you to hazards ahead. This sign warns you that wet pavement can be slippery. Drive slowly and carefully.

questions.question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?

options.text: Start to prepare to slow down.
Sound a sharp blast of your horn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
questions.explanation: Use a sharp horn blast to warn a child or pedestrian who is about to enter the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: A driver's left arm and hand are extended downward. What does this hand signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: When a driver extends their left arm and hand downward, they are signaling that they plan to stop. Adjust your driving if you are following this driver.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn your wheels to the right.
Turn your wheels to the left.
Keep your wheels pointed straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your wheels to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply to the right when parking downhill. If your car rolls, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign with black markings tells you that traffic may merge from the right. Be ready to let other cars safely merge into your lane.

questions.question: You are approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light. What should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait for the light to change.
Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.
Prepare to stop; the light is about to turn red.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive carefully through the intersection.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means proceed slowly and carefully. Look both ways before crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad ahead.
questions.explanation: A round yellow sign warns you that a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: When you plan to pass another vehicle, what should you remember?

options.text: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.
Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you space or the right-of-way, even if you signal. Always check that it is safe before passing.

questions.question: Why is it important to watch for motorcycles?

options.text: They are harder to see than cars.
Motorcycle riders are less skilled than other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: They are harder to see than cars.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are smaller and harder to see than cars. They can hide in your blind spot. It is hard to judge how far away a motorcycle is and how fast it is going. Always pay extra attention when near motorcycles.

questions.question: What is a safe way to drive through a curve?

options.text: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
Keep the same speed through the whole curve.
Speed up as you enter, slow down as you exit.
Stay near the right edge of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you enter, speed up as you exit.
questions.explanation: Slow down before you enter a curve. Speed up gradually as you leave the curve. If you speed up while entering a curve, it will be harder to control your car.

questions.question: On a multilane, one-way street or highway, which lane should you use to turn left?
questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: Use the left lane to turn left from multilane streets and highways.

questions.question: When parking uphill on a hill with a curb, how should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them sharply toward the curb.
Turn them slightly to the right.
Turn them sharply away from the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them sharply away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels sharply away from the curb when parking uphill. This stops your car from rolling into traffic if your brakes fail. If there is no curb, turn your wheels sharply toward the edge of the road.

questions.question: A traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Treat it like a caution sign and keep going through the intersection.
Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
Speed up to get through before the red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection, unless you are too close to stop safely.
questions.explanation: When you see a yellow light at an intersection, slow down and try to stop before you enter it, if it is safe. If you cannot stop safely, drive carefully through the intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for traffic on your right.
Don't park on the right side of the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a line through a symbol means that action is not allowed. In this case, the symbol shows a right turn, so no right turn is allowed.

questions.question: When driving to a place you don't know, what should you do?

options.text: Rely on road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you leave.
Just know the general direction of your destination.
Always take the most direct route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you leave.
questions.explanation: Plan your route before you start driving to an unfamiliar place. Do not start driving with just a rough idea of where you are going. Check the location on a map first.

questions.question: You and another driver arrive at a four-way stop at the same time. The other driver is on your left. Who has the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: You have the right-of-way.
questions.explanation: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, the vehicle to the right has the right-of-way.

questions.question: Why should you be careful when passing a bicycle?

options.text: You are moving faster than the bicycle.
The bicycle always has the right-of-way.
Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass.
The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The cyclist may swerve into traffic to avoid something on the road.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing a bicycle because the rider may have to swerve into traffic to avoid an object in the road. Always drive carefully near cyclists.

questions.question: If your car starts to skid, which way should you turn the steering wheel?

options.text: In the direction you want the car to go.
In the opposite direction of the skid.
In any direction. It doesn't matter.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the direction you want the car to go.
questions.explanation: Turn the steering wheel in the direction you want the car to go if it starts to skid. Once the car starts to straighten out, turn the wheel back the other way.
